name: ProactBench
description: ProactBench is a benchmark for measuring conversational proactivity in multi-turn LLM dialogues. It decomposes proactivity into three phase-tied trigger types (Emergent, Critical, Recovery) and evaluates them with an offline LLM judge that scores model responses against per-trigger rubrics authored prospectively at curation time. The released corpus contains 198 curated dialogues with 624 trigger points across 5 persona categories and 24 communication styles drawn from the Communication Styles Inventory (CSI), produced by a five-stage internal curation pipeline; only the final curated corpus (final_dialogues.jsonl) is distributed in this release.
citeAs: @inproceedings{anonymous2026proactbench, title={ProactBench: Beyond What The User Asked For}, author={Anonymous}, booktitle={Under review at NeurIPS 2026}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Dialogues are synthetically generated by a three-agent pipeline. Personas are sampled from Nemotron-Personas-USA (NVIDIA, CC-BY-4.0). For each (persona, category) pair, a Planner LLM generates a proactive scenario with a hidden goal, explicit surface request, implicit anchors, and ideal trajectory. Scenarios are expanded into turn-by-turn blueprints under each of 24 CSI communication styles. Blueprints pass an independent-LLM-judge audit (different model family from the Planner) before inclusion. The full three-agent loop then runs once per validated blueprint to produce the final dialogue corpus. See the paper Section 3 and the README for full pipeline details.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Trigger-point rubrics are authored prospectively by the Planner at turn t, before the assistant has generated its response at turn t+1. Each rubric specifies pass / partial / fail criteria grounded in the anchors disclosed by turn t. The released benchmark scoring is performed at run time by an offline LLM judge (default GPT-5.4) that, for each (evaluated_model, dialogue) pair, regenerates the assistant response at every trigger turn and scores it against the committed rubric using only the dialogue history; the judge receives no persona, communication-style, or planner state. Each judge label includes a verbatim evidence quote from the response and a free-text rationale. Two Prolific human-validation studies described in the paper bound judge reliability (Krippendorff alpha = 0.69 ordinal on Study 1 with n=275 ratings / 18 raters; pairwise B-preference 0.80 over 144 non-tie comparisons on Study 2 with n=146 ratings / 8 raters).
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Per-trigger-type pass rates and weighted scores (PASS=1.0, PARTIAL=0.5, FAIL=0.0) are reported across 16 evaluated models in the paper. A judge-swap ablation across three judges (GPT-5.4, Claude-Opus-4.7, Kimi-K2.6) shows pairwise Cohen's kappa of 0.35-0.46 on overall trigger labels, with model rankings preserved (Spearman rho 0.64-0.89). Two human-validation studies bound judge reliability against humans (Study 1: Krippendorff alpha = 0.69 across 18 raters on a 60-item stratified sample; Study 2: pairwise B-preference 0.80 [0.74, 0.86] across 144 non-tie comparisons on 80 stratified Recovery items).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dialogues that fail to complete the minimum 5-turn requirement or that fail blueprint validation are excluded from the corpus. The released corpus has 198 dialogues that all complete >=5 turns with at least 2 trigger points each.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be hosted at an anonymous URL during peer review (HuggingFace Datasets after acceptance, with the same Apache-2.0 license). Updates and corrections will be tracked via the GitHub repository's release tags.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating large language models on conversational proactivity; comparing model behaviour at different conversational phases (Emergent / Critical / Recovery); studying robustness to user communication style variation; calibration of LLM-as-judge agreement.
rai:dataLimitations: All dialogues are in English; personas are US-based (sourced from Nemotron-Personas-USA). Norms around unsolicited advice and initiative-taking differ across cultures, so ProactBench scores should not be used to guide deployment beyond US-English contexts. The benchmark uses a single seed model (Gemini-2.5-Pro) for the curation phase, so absolute pass rates should be interpreted relative to that fixed seed; rankings are robust across cross-family judge-swaps but absolute magnitudes can shift. The scenario base is 25 (persona, category) scenarios drawn from 19 personas, expanded across 24 communication styles; per-(model, style) cell sizes are accordingly small (~8 dialogues per style on average). Offline scoring re-uses the curation model's conversation history; an alternative-curation ablation in the paper bounds this effect but does not eliminate it. The GPT-5.4-authored rubric is the single point of subjective interpretation; cross-family judge-swap and human-validation studies are reported as bounds.
rai:syntheticDataDescription: The entire ProactBench dialogue corpus is synthetic. Personas are sampled from Nemotron-Personas-USA (NVIDIA, CC-BY-4.0), itself a synthetic persona dataset generated from a probabilistic graphical model conditioned on US Census demographics. Scenarios, blueprints, and dialogues are produced by a three-agent LLM pipeline (Planner, User Agent, Assistant Model); see rai:dataCollection. No real-user conversations, transcripts, or behavioural data are collected, scraped, or redistributed in this release.
rai:dataBiases: Personas are sampled from a US-English distribution and the Communication Styles Inventory was developed primarily in workplace contexts; the benchmark may be biased toward Western professional communication norms. The Planner and offline judge are both GPT-5.4 in the main configuration, raising the possibility of stylistic self-affinity (mitigated by the cross-family judge-swap ablation reported in the paper).
rai:dataSocialImpact: ProactBench measures whether LLMs can take grounded, anchor-specific initiative in dialogue. Higher proactivity scores should not be interpreted as a universal objective: unsolicited suggestions can be helpful or intrusive depending on user preferences, privacy context, and task criticality. We treat ProactBench as a capability probe, not a training target in isolation; production deployment decisions should weigh proactivity alongside explicit user preferences and domain-specific appropriateness.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive real-user information is included. Personas are synthetic (derived from Nemotron-Personas-USA, which is itself a synthetic persona dataset).

prov:wasDerivedFrom.name: Nemotron-Personas-USA
prov:wasDerivedFrom.description: Synthetic persona dataset by NVIDIA (CC-BY-4.0), generated from a probabilistic graphical model conditioned on US Census demographics. Used as the source of 50 sampled personas.

prov:wasGeneratedBy.name: ProactBench five-stage curation pipeline
prov:wasGeneratedBy.description: Stage 1: Sample 50 personas from Nemotron-Personas-USA and generate 500 candidate scenarios (10 per persona) via Planner LLM. Stage 2: Curate 25 (persona, category) scenarios drawn from 19 personas, stratified at 5 per life-domain category. Stage 3: Render each scenario across 10 of 24 CSI communication styles into turn-by-turn blueprints (250 total). Stage 4: Independent-judge audit (different model family) filters to 207 validated blueprints. Stage 5: Three-agent loop (Planner, User Agent, Assistant Model) produces 198 released dialogues with 624 trigger points. Only the Stage 5 output (final_dialogues.jsonl) is redistributed in this release; the offline-evaluation pipeline shipped with this dataset re-runs each dialogue against any user-supplied evaluated model and scores responses at every trigger turn against the embedded Planner-authored rubric.

distribution.name: final_dialogues.jsonl
distribution.description: Main corpus: 198 curated dialogues with 624 trigger points (201 EMERGENT / 232 CRITICAL / 191 RECOVERY). Each row carries the full ten-turn record, the trigger schedule, and the Planner-authored rubrics. The benchmark proper.

recordSet.name: dialogues
recordSet.description: One record per curated dialogue (198 rows). Each contains the full multi-turn conversation, trigger points with rubrics, and token usage.

field.name: unique_id_eval
field.description: Composite unique identifier formatted as `{blueprint_id}__style{style_combination_index}__{uuid}`. Guaranteed unique across the corpus and used as the primary key for joining with offline-evaluation outputs.

field.name: blueprint_id
field.description: Identifier of the blueprint this dialogue was rolled out from (e.g. `BP_PROFESSIONAL_01_EVA`).

field.name: style_combination_index
field.description: Index into the 24-style CSI factorial (1-24). See Appendix C of the paper.

field.name: evaluated_model
field.description: Identifier of the model whose responses populated the dialogue at curation time (Gemini-2.5-Pro for the released corpus).

field.name: num_turns_completed
field.description: Number of turns reached before the dialogue terminated. Min 5, max 10.

field.name: trigger_points
field.description: JSON-encoded array of trigger-point records. Each carries the trigger turn index and the rubric (pass/partial/fail criteria authored by the Planner before the model responded). No curation-time judge output is included in the released main corpus; per-model scored outputs (responses, scores, rationales, evidence quotes) live in the eval_results FileSet.

field.name: turn_records
field.description: JSON-encoded array of turn records: planner state, user message, assistant response.

field.name: token_usage
field.description: JSON-encoded per-agent token usage (planner, user_agent, assistant).
